what_it_did.what_the_split_means: A mechanical commit republishes an unchanged net -- the report, the dashboard, the state files. Counting those as work would make a quiet day look busy, so they are separated rather than filtered: they happened, they are just not progress.

what_it_decided.thesis_read: Three hours, four commits, all substantive, and the two that matter both landed against the top of the last direction record: the baseline now exists as an external fact rather than this company's own habit, and the publish outage was diagnosed to a real cause. The baseline is the bigger of the two. Ofgem's own EBIT decision says an efficient supplier earns GBP 3.73-8.54/MWh on this book; the flat control was GBP 2.00, about a quarter of that at the top of the range. The director's frame said "it performed well" means nothing without a credible control, and the control is now credible and independently sourced. But the same measurement destroyed the more comfortable story: the value arm's median choice is GBP 130/MWh, which is fifteen times the TOP of what the regulator allows. Repricing the control moves it by two to four times and leaves the arm an order of magnitude away, so the arm is not beating a straw man -- it is asking to charge many times what a regulated efficient supplier earns, on 213 of 263 accounts, and it says `fit_to_run: false` about itself. The belief is no longer the excuse: the median account is now scored +3.5pp CONSERVATIVE against what the world would actually do. So the honest read is that the per-customer machinery, the world that can punish it, and the control to judge it against all now exist -- and the decision that machinery produces is not one any supplier would make. The advantage still cannot be claimed, and the reason has moved from "we cannot measure it" to "the answer is visibly wrong", which is progress. Two things are drifting and both are mechanical. The publish repair raised the commit deadline from 600s to 840s and its own commit message said the number was the small half of the change; the very next episode still did not land, 811 seconds after its own scoped gate went green, and publishing is now down 13 hours. That is a second strike on one component (R3) and the answer is not a third number. And the mechanism that makes this record reachable at all -- LANE 0, its supervisor wiring, its tests -- is running from the working tree and is in NO COMMIT: git has never seen `background/delivery_lane.py`, yet the supervisor logged six LANE 0 draws from it this evening. On the previous focus: the orienting brief reports that none of it was drawn. That is the instrument being wrong, not the steer -- it counts maturity-map atom draws only, so the two items that DID land, by hand, are invisible to it. The steer is not a no-op; it is unmeasured. What IS true is that every ordinary draw is livelocked: all five BUILD candidates are stalled, EP1 at 268 consecutive draws without its level moving, and all 24 idle atoms are over the discovery pass ceiling. Naming an atom is therefore no longer enough on its own -- the draw already picks these constantly and nothing moves. Every item below is written as an instruction for that reason.

focus.what: In `company/pricing/value_based_renewal.py`, diagnose why expected value rises monotonically in margin across the whole region the churn model supports, so the "choice" is whichever bound binds first -- 165 of 263 accounts support-bound, 8 at the grid edge, 107 landing on the identical GBP 130/MWh. Fix the arithmetic so the chosen margin is interior and set by that customer's own switching response, or state with evidence that no interior optimum exists and what the arm must do then.
focus.why: This is the organ the whole thesis rests on, and right now it is not making a per-customer decision -- it is charging the maximum its model will permit and reporting the ceiling as an inference. Done when the record shows chosen margins set by the customer rather than by the bound, and `fit_to_run` says something other than "a ceiling reporting itself as a decision".

what_next.why_this_is_here: Direction multiplies the draw's existing weights and can never zero one, so it can only ever be ignored -- never obeyed by force. Whether it was actually followed is therefore a measurement, not an assumption.

how_to_read_this: The delivery seat wakes on a timer, reads the last stretch, and writes direction -- never code. What it decides biases which work the ticks draw and can never block any of it. Everything on this page is read from a committed record; nothing here is computed a second time.
